170	def _shell_payload(command: SimpleCommand, args: list[str], ctx: _Context,
171	                   nested: Callable[..., None]) -> None:
172	    """`bash -c STR` (and fish's command options), and a script read from stdin:
173	    `bash <<EOF`, `bash <<< STR`, `bash < file`, `echo STR | bash`,
174	    `cat file | bash`, `bash -s args < file`."""
175	    shell = shell_invocation(command.name, args)
176	    if shell.syntax_only:
177	        return  # `-n`: read and syntax-check only, never execute
178	    if command.name == "bash":
179	        # A non-interactive bash first runs the file $BASH_ENV names, `bash -c` included.
180	        for value in command.env_values("BASH_ENV"):
181	            for path in _startup_paths(value, command, ctx):
182	                _run_file(path, command, ctx, nested)
183	    if command.name == "bash" and shell.interactive:
184	        if shell.startup_file:
185	            if "$" in shell.startup_file or "`" in shell.startup_file:
186	                ctx.result.truncated = True
187	                ctx.result.skipped_sources.append((command, "bash rc file"))
188	            else:
189	                _run_file(shell.startup_file, command, ctx, nested)
190	        _interactive_hooks(command, nested)
191	    if _xtrace_option(_leading_options(args)):
192	        # `bash -x`: the child traces from its first command, expanding $PS4.
193	        for value in command.env_values("PS4"):
194	            nested(_prompt_expansion(value), f"{command.name} -x PS4")
195	    if shell.interactive and _reads_env_file(command.name, args):
196	        # An interactive POSIX shell first runs the file $ENV names (PR review).
197	        for value in command.env_values("ENV"):
198	            for path in _startup_paths(value, command, ctx):
199	                _run_file(path, command, ctx, nested)
200	    prelude = _option_prelude(command.name, args)
201	    for text in shell.commands:
202	        nested(prelude + _bind_positionals(text, list(shell.command_args)), f"{command.name} -c")
203	    if shell.script:
204	        _produced_script(shell.script, command, ctx, nested)  # `bash <(echo CMD)`
205	    if not shell.reads_stdin:
206	        return  # a command string or a script file (shell_sources resolves the file)
207	    # Redirections apply in order: the shell reads only the last one to stdin,
208	    # which also replaces a pipe (`bash <<< 'rm -rf x' <<< :` runs only `:`).
209	    stdin = [r for r in command.redirects if r.op in _STDIN_OPERATORS and (r.fd is None or r.fd == 0)]
210	    if stdin:
211	        _stdin_script(stdin[-1], command, ctx, nested)
212	        return
213	    feeder = ctx.result.previous_stage(command)
214	    if feeder is None or feeder.dynamic_head:
215	        return
216	    if feeder.name in ("echo", "printf"):
217	        text = _echoed_text(feeder)
218	        if text:
219	            nested(text, f"{feeder.name} | {command.name}")
220	    elif feeder.name == "cat":
221	        # `cat a.sh b.sh | bash` runs each file just like `bash a.sh`; `cat <<EOF | bash`
222	        # (or `cat -u - <<EOF`) passes cat's own stdin on unchanged.
223	        passed = [r for r in feeder.redirects if r.op in _STDIN_OPERATORS and (r.fd is None or r.fd == 0)]
224	        for operand in _cat_operands(feeder.args) or ["-"]:
225	            if operand not in STDIN_PATHS:
226	                _run_file(operand, command, ctx, nested)
227	            elif passed:
228	                _stdin_script(passed[-1], command, ctx, nested)

231	def _cat_operands(args: tuple[str, ...]) -> list[str]:
232	    """cat's files; its options (`-u`, `-v`, `--show-all`) take no value."""
233	    found: list[str] = []
234	    ended = False
235	    for arg in args:
236	        if ended or arg == "-" or not arg.startswith("-"):
237	            found.append(arg)
238	        elif arg == "--":
239	            ended = True
240	    return found

254	def _set_option(args: list[str], option: str) -> bool:
255	    """`bash -o posix`: the option is set (a later `+o posix` unsets it)."""
256	    state = False
257	    for index, arg in enumerate(args[:-1]):
258	        if arg in ("-o", "+o") and args[index + 1] == option:
259	            state = arg == "-o"

263	def _xtrace_option(args: list[str]) -> bool | None:
264	    """What `set ARGS` does to xtrace: True for `-x`/`-o xtrace`, False for
265	    `+x`/`+o xtrace`, None when it is not mentioned. The last mention wins."""
266	    state: bool | None = None
267	    for index, arg in enumerate(args):
268	        if arg in ("--", "-"):
269	            break
270	        if arg in ("-o", "+o") and index + 1 < len(args) and args[index + 1] == "xtrace":
271	            state = arg == "-o"
272	        elif len(arg) > 1 and arg[0] in "-+" and arg[1] != "-" and "x" in arg[1:]:
273	            state = arg[0] == "-"
274	        elif not arg.startswith(("-", "+")) and (index == 0 or args[index - 1] not in ("-o", "+o")):
275	            break  # the positional parameters start here
276	    return state

findings.explanation: This change makes the guard follow GNU chmod's reading of dash modes such as `-w+s`. GNU chmod does not stop at the first dash mode, though. It collects every dash-mode argument and joins them with commas. getopt also reorders arguments, so dash modes placed after file operands still count. chmod_dash_mode returns only the first match, and _chmod_dangerous judges only that one mode. A harmless first mode therefore hides a dangerous later one. With `chmod -x -u+s /usr/local/bin/x`, GNU applies `-x,-u+s` (setuid), but the guard checks only `-x` and allows it. The same happens with `chmod -x /usr/local/bin/x -u+s`. World-writable variants work too, for example `chmod -x -o+w /etc` and `chmod -r -w=rwx /etc`.
findings.fix: Collect every argument that matches _CHMOD_DASH_MODE, before and after operands (GNU reading), stopping at `--`. Join them with ',' to form the effective mode, and run _setuid and _world_writable on the combined mode. Also keep the BSD reading, where the first operand is the mode, and deny if either reading is dangerous.

findings.explanation: _cat_operands drops every dash-prefixed argument that comes before `--`, wherever it appears, which matches GNU getopt's reordering. BSD/macOS cat (this repo runs on darwin) stops reading options at the first operand, so later dash-prefixed arguments are files whose contents go into the pipe. For example, in `cat ./a.sh -payload | sh`, BSD cat outputs the file `-payload` to sh. The guard never calls _run_file on that file, so its contents are not checked for dangerous commands. Such a file could have been written earlier, e.g. `printf 'rm -rf ~' > ./-payload`.
findings.fix: After the first operand, treat every later argument as an operand (the BSD reading), or analyse both readings. In particular, pass any dash-prefixed argument that follows an operand to _run_file.
